assumptions: Root cause confirmed empirically with @vitest/coverage-v8: lcov emits one DA line per statement, so continuation lines of a multi-line statement are absent from the measured set; the fix scores them by that statement's recorded line instead of reading absence as non-executable.

The judgement is lexical (open ( [ or object-literal {, trailing/leading operators, multi-line template literals), not a TypeScript parse: the engine has no runtime typescript dependency. Errors lean toward 'executable' (a noisy finding) rather than 'non-executable' (a hidden gap).

The #841 object-literal shape that #928 pinned as non-coverable is the same false-green class and is reclassified when source is readable; the #928 fixture (no source on disk) still pins the no-source fallback.
When the changed file's source cannot be read at repoRoot, only recorded lines are scored (pre-#1314 behaviour), rather than treating every unmeasured line as coverable.

The lexer lives in a new sub-module ts/src/guardian/diff-coverage/lexical/ (precedent: diff-coverage/formats/) so diff-coverage/ stays under its 1800-LOC module-size ceiling; it reuses type-only.ts's stripComments/stepQuote/QUOTES, which are now exported.

report-tier.ts is left unchanged (it sits at the 300-line perf cap and its coupling ratio is at the limit): the orchestrator passes matchUnitsToIndex a copied index in which each continuation line is folded into the file's measured set, carrying the hits of its statement's recorded line.
